$comment: Curated half of the YFex Atlas. Edit by hand (or ask an agent). The scanner (C:\Dev\Scripts\yfexAtlas.cs) merges this with what it finds on disk and writes atlas.data.js + atlas.generated.json. Statuses: idea, proposed, approved, building, integrating, done, prototype, residue, domain.

groups.name: Foundation
groups.summary: Core types and the small generic building blocks everything else stands on.

groups.name: Identity & Trust
groups.summary: Who is there, what they may do, which machine it is, keys, privacy and licences.

groups.name: Data & State
groups.summary: Local app state, SQL access and schemas, reactive state, event streams, search.

groups.name: Messaging & Workflow
groups.summary: Commands, events, RPC, validation and rules, sagas, jobs, outbound HTTP, messages to people, files.

groups.name: Operations & Platform
groups.summary: Observability, audit, network, offline sites, hosting, installing, machine and device access.

groups.name: UI & Tooling
groups.summary: Controls, navigation, MVVM glue, discoverable actions and developer tools.

groups.name: Domain (out of scope)
groups.summary: Product and business repos. Consumers of the infrastructure; excluded from the analysis.

components.name: YFex core
components.summary: Types-only base every library may reference: value objects (Money, Quantity, EmailAddress, PhoneNumber, MacAddress), Hash256/KeyId/DetachedSignature, Installations/Time/Networking/Privacy/Offline types, YFex.Diagnostics probes (Operations, LogWriter), Localization catalogs, Consent.
components.next: Receive actor types (⚑RA8) and decide ScopeIdentity; keep logic out.
pending: ⚑RA9–RA11 actor types in core (grant, one ActorKind numbering, namespace)

components.name: Expressions
components.summary: Expression language extracted from Rules.Dynamic (parser, evaluator, generator). Leaf; Composer is the planned second consumer.
components.next: Verify X.0–X.4 in the real tree (memory says unverified).

components.name: Xml
components.summary: Source-generated XML serialization (AOT-safe), used by fiscal XML generation.
components.next: No design doc or status: add a README with scope and status.

components.name: Resilience
components.summary: Retry / timeout / circuit-breaker policy vocabulary (ResilienceSpec as a cheap record struct) with an optional Polly adapter.
components.next: Every retry in the ecosystem uses its vocabulary since 2026-11-05 (F04); stored retries use RetryDelay + RetryBudget.

components.name: Actors
components.summary: One actor model for every library and app: ActorKind, ActorIdentity (text form + canonical bytes), ActorScope, ambient ActorContext with capture/restore for stored work, ActorStamp, ActorClaims, IActorDirectory contracts. Leaf above core.
components.next: AC1: move Authorization.Public, Audit, Offline, Authentication, Messaging, Cqrs, NavigatR, Capabilities, Jobs, Search onto it and delete the old actor types (closes F05).

components.name: Time
components.summary: Trusted time: pluggable sources (central anchor, NTP, HTTPS date, authority, GNSS, peers), monotonic clock, high-water mark, rollback detection; registers a TimeProvider.
components.next: Adoption by apps (UseTpmClock, AuthenticateHighWater, signed central anchor); Linux TPM clock; Roughtime/NTS (⚑T15).

components.name: Tenancy
components.summary: Scope identity (ScopeIdentity: tenant → site → …), scope resolution from requests/claims, scoped overrides.
components.next: Decide whether ScopeIdentity (the value) moves to core so libraries stop needing per-library .Tenancy adapters (F18).

components.name: CustomLogic
components.summary: Per-scope implementation selection: descriptors, registry and generated declarations pick a tenant/site-specific implementation of a service or handler.
components.next: P2 (NavigatR) and P3 (Avalonia).

components.name: Cryptography
components.summary: The one crypto library: key rings and rotation, root-key providers (CNG/TPM, Linux TPM/Secret Service, Apple, Android Keystore), sealed values, MACs, signatures, recipient sealing incl. hybrid ML-KEM, CA and certificates, hash chains/Merkle, secret stores, XML-DSig.
components.next: Run .Linux/.Apple on their OS (14 §8), Android real handheld, adoption Phase 4 (Audit, Privacy).

components.name: Authentication
components.summary: Proves who: accounts per realm, passwords/PIN/codes (e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp), Google/Microsoft/OIDC, sessions and ES256 tokens, MFA/step-up, desktop client and offline bridge. Never decides permissions.
components.next: AN-P6 passkeys; P3 leftovers. Put the repo under git.

components.name: Authorization
components.summary: Decides what: permission catalogs, one CompiledPolicy per message, gates for CQRS/RPC/HTTP/routes/VM commands, signed snapshots for offline, approval tokens, impersonation, site presence.
components.next: Phase 4c approval-policy table.

components.name: Installations
components.summary: Which installed copy is this, and is that machine one of ours: enrollment, TPM keys, tenant CA certificates, signed rosters and bundles, peer channels (friends), site mesh, pairing, Android handhelds.
components.next: I6 acceptance on a real handheld; ⚑I24 site-tag key, ⚑I42–I44.

components.name: Privacy
components.summary: Data classification on value-object types ([Sensitive], DataSensitivity in core), masks, scrubbing; later consent by purpose, pseudonyms, crypto-shredding and data-subject rights.
components.next: Tier 1 done 2026-11-05 (TextScrubber, logging Redaction, IExtractable, PropertyRedactor in Profiling, Web credential and PortableSecretStore leaks) except the UI mask presenter (last). Next: Phase 2 Pseudonymizer (Profiling hashing, logging Hash mode). Runtime types live in core; the repo holds the generator and the runtime engines.

components.name: Licensing
components.summary: Vendor-signed licences on top of Installations: products, modules (= permission sets), seats, activation lists, trusted-time expiry and grace, Authorization masking.
components.next: Answer ⚑LC1–LC22.

components.name: Capabilities
components.summary: One manifest of every actionable/queryable surface (view models, CQRS messages) for the search bar, AI agents and visibility. Reads permissions, never grants them.
components.next: Localizer over core IMessageCatalog (F12); refresh design-doc status.

components.name: Persistence
components.summary: Local app-state storage: IKeyValueStore, durable queues, caches; SQLite/IndexedDB/file-system backends; encryption at rest; tenancy adapter; generator.
components.next: Make Persistence.Encryption OS-neutral (F03 / auto platform-leak).

components.name: Data
components.summary: Database access: connections, dialects, query builder, generated row mapping, IBulkWriter, portable schema modules + migrator, row-level security, EF bridge; engines Sqlite/Postgres/SqlServer/Oracle.
components.next: DS-P7 (optional live verification, fifth engine).

components.name: DataMining
components.summary: Data discovery/mapping/migration engine between arbitrary databases and files (evidence → hypotheses, YAML-driven), with CSV/Excel/Mongo connectors, API and CLI. A sub-product inside the Data repo.
components.next: Decide whether it is infrastructure or a product; align connector names (YFex.Csv → YFex.DataMining.Csv).

components.name: State
components.summary: Generated reactive state objects (bitmap change tracking), collections, undo/redo history (+persistence), MVVM and Blazor adapters.

components.name: EventSourcing
components.summary: Event-sourced aggregates over IKeyValueStore (client/offline/AOT) or Marten (server), projections, snapshots, offline stream sync, generated folds and handlers.
components.next: Design doc still says Proposed; Marten provider builds outside the solution.

components.name: Search
components.summary: Provider-neutral universal search orchestration (normalized score + intent + frecency), permission-filtered, with a Capabilities source.
components.next: Finish V0.

components.name: Validation
components.summary: Shape validation: generated, pure, sync validators for DTOs/commands/view models; violations, constraints, message catalogs.
components.next: Phase 5 Avalonia UI (last; needs a reusable grid design).

components.name: Rules
components.summary: Pure business-rule engine over typed Situations: rule sets, stages, decision tables, directives, traces; dynamic JSON rules, SQL rule store, admin/what-if.
components.next: Phase 6A Fiscal (deferred by the user).

components.name: Cqrs
components.summary: Commands/queries contracts, aggregate configuration, generated dispatch, pipeline stages (validation, rules, authorization, approvals, compensation, tenancy).
components.next: Retry is on Resilience since 2026-11-05 (F04).

components.name: Messaging
components.summary: In-process event bus, Fusion (state ↔ bus), RPC with offline outbox, call context, server-pushed events, Wolverine bridge.
components.next: Reference Authorization.Public instead of the engine (auto finding).

components.name: Orchestration
components.summary: Sagas, process managers, durable waits/timers, compensation walk, inbox and dead-letter policy; RPC + Wolverine transports.
components.next: Design doc still says nothing is built; share timers/inbox with Jobs/EventSourcing (F09, F10).

components.name: Jobs
components.summary: Embedded source-generated job scheduler ([Job]), three-mode ladder with Hub governance (B) and Worker (C), user-defined job templates (D) with secrets, history, notifier, capabilities.
components.next: D2b run-as waits for actor types in core (⚑RA8/RA9) and Audit/Authorization steps.

components.name: Web
components.summary: Outbound HTTP API clients (Refit): per-scope endpoints and credentials, token handling, sealed secrets in SQL (Web.Data), ASP.NET Core glue.
components.next: Move ISecretProtector to Cryptography (F08); confirm the web-tenancy plan status.

components.name: Notifications
components.summary: One way to send messages to people: e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp, chat, webhooks, in-app, push; providers, contact book, templates over core catalogs, durable outbox, inbound receipts.
components.next: Answer ⚑N1–N20 (N14, N17 agreed). Absorbs Authentication.Delivery transports, Logging alert channels, Jobs IJobNotifier.

components.name: Files
components.summary: Remote file stores behind one IFileStore (folders, FTP/FTPS, SFTP, S3, Azure Blob) + partner Exchange (inbox/outbox, claim once, ledger, zip).
components.next: Answer ⚑F2–F22.

components.name: Logging
components.summary: Opt-in observability engine: libraries probe YFex.Diagnostics in core; the engine adds pooled MPSC pipeline, sinks, sampling, metrics, bridges, scrubbing.
components.next: Phase 2 (handoff in 10); adopt InstallationId for node identity (F06).

components.name: Audit
components.summary: Lossless, tamper-evident audit trail: who did what to which data under which tenant and approval. .Public contracts + engine + [AuditChanges] generator.
components.next: Cqrs .Audit() stage, durable journal (⚑A13), hash chains/anchors on Cryptography, server/store; A8–A14.

components.name: Networking
components.summary: Network conditions, reachability, diagnostics (DNS, traceroute, TLS check), LAN discovery (beacons, mDNS, SSDP, WS-Discovery), Telnet, SNMP. Finds candidates; never decides trust.
components.next: Phase 7 Survey package; ⚑N29 macOS.

components.name: Offline
components.summary: Offline operating model: modes, site broker, signed offline envelopes, offline sign-in, site manifest/limits/allowances, signed rule data, central reconciliation, durable stores.
components.next: Phase 4 (broker services on Installations peer channels; needs Hosting H0 for 4f), Phase 5.

components.name: Hosting
components.summary: One service host per machine role (yfex-host): module catalog, profiles from central via Tenancy/Installations, control channel, CLI, tray (last).
components.next: H0 (needed by Offline 4f); ⚑H8, ⚑H11–H22.

components.name: Installer
components.summary: Install, enroll, firewall rules, service install, self-update with vendor-signed packages and site broker cache. Built after everything else.
components.next: Orientation only; ⚑IN1–IN8.

components.name: Automation
components.summary: Layered desktop + AI automation engine (Plans A–H): task graphs, orchestrator, Windows input/observation, AI agents (API, reversed, desktop), secret and session stores.
components.next: Moved under C:\Dev\YFex 2026-11-05; secrets now sealed with YFex.Cryptography (YFex.Automation.Secrets); git initialized 2026-11-05 (no remote yet).

components.name: System
components.summary: Consent-gated machine telemetry: hardware/OS/network snapshots (Windows provider).
components.next: Hand NetworkSnapshot over to Networking; unsalted MAC hash (privacy F-list).

components.name: Profiling
components.summary: Consent-aware user-behaviour profile signals with offline queue and a Windows provider; UI hooks.
components.next: Hashing through Privacy/Cryptography (salted HMAC), consent by purpose.

components.name: Security
components.summary: Security intelligence and inspection: packet capture/interception (Windows), analysis, CLI and an elevated service.
components.next: Separate elevated service installed by Installer (⚑H6).

components.name: Devices
components.summary: Hardware toolkit: inventory, drivers, own serial/COM, virtual COM (incl. UMDF driver), firmware, protocols (Modbus, SCPI, NMEA, AT), POS peripherals, remoting, Bluetooth.
components.next: Linux project later; remoting trust via Installations instead of PSK.

components.name: UI

components.next: Delete the duplicate core YFex.UI.Abstractions (F11).

components.name: NavigatR

components.name: Mvvm

findings.resolution: 2026-11-05: framework folders moved to sibling repos YFex.Cqrs, YFex.Messaging (incl. Cqrs.Approvals, Rules.Admin), YFex.NavigatR, YFex.Persistence, YFex.Validation, YFex.Rules, YFex.State, YFex.Expressions, YFex.Mvvm. Core repo now references nothing outside itself. Remaining repo cycles: F28, F29.
findings.title: The core repo is not a leaf: it references satellite repos that reference it back
findings.detail: Projects in the YFex repo (Cqrs, Messaging.Rpc, Rules, Rules.Data, NavigatR, Persistence.Encryption, Mvvm, Cqrs.Approvals/Tenancy) reference Authorization(.Public), Tenancy, Cryptography(.Windows), Time, Resilience, YFex.Data and YFex.UI.Public — and all of those reference YFex core. There is no project-level cycle, but the repositories form a cycle, so they cannot be versioned, built or published as independent NuGet packages in any order. The auto findings 'Repository cycle' and 'Core repo depends on satellites' list every edge.
findings.recommendation: Treat the YFex repo as two things: the types-only core (leaf) and a set of framework components (Cqrs, Messaging, Rules, NavigatR, State, Persistence, Mvvm). Move the few contracts the framework needs (Permission, ActorIdentity, ScopeIdentity, ResilienceSpec) into core types (extends ⚑RA8), or move the framework components to their own repos. Then enforce 'core repo references nothing outside itself' with an architecture test.

findings.resolution: 2026-11-04: Web.Refit moved onto Resilience (UseResilience; RetryHandler/RetryOptions deleted). 2026-11-05: Cqrs RetryPolicy/BackoffStrategy/RetryConfigurationBuilder deleted (.Retry takes YFex.Resilience.RetryPolicy or int; no-op query .Retry removed). Resilience gained RetryBudget + the Polly-free RetryDelay calculator for stored retries; Jobs RetryPolicy class deleted, [Retry]/settings/store/generator use Resilience types, RetryCalculator and Hub ReconnectBackoff call RetryDelay (fixed x2, jitter +-20%, clean storage break). Orchestration RetryThenDeadLetterPolicy kept: a redelivery count, not backoff. Notifications/Files plans already route retries through Resilience.
findings.title: Retry/backoff is implemented five times next to YFex.Resilience
findings.detail: Resilience.RetryPolicy (Policies.cs) vs Cqrs RetryPolicy + RetryConfigurationBuilder (YFex.Cqrs/src/YFex.Cqrs/RetryPolicy.cs — Cqrs already references Resilience), Jobs RetryPolicy/RetryCalculator/[Retry], Jobs Hub ReconnectBackoff, Web.Refit RetryHandler/RetryOptions (+ its own docs/07-resilience.md), Orchestration RetryThenDeadLetterPolicy. Files and Notifications plan a sixth and seventh.
findings.recommendation: Resilience owns the vocabulary (retry spec, backoff + jitter calculator, classification of transient failures) as pure types; Cqrs/Jobs/Web/Orchestration map their configuration onto it. Write it into the Files and Notifications plans before they are built.

findings.resolution: 2026-11-05: plan written (docs/internal/actors, PROPOSED): new package YFex.Actors (user decision), Audit numbering, clean break. 2026-11-05: AC0 BUILT — repo YFex.Actors (ActorKind in Audit numbering, ActorIdentity + text form + canonical bytes, ActorScope, ActorContext with Capture/Restore + ActorSnapshot, ActorStamp, ActorClaims, directory contracts; 134 tests, AOT smoke clean, 0-allocation format/canonical paths). Consumers not moved yet: AC1 moves Authorization/Audit/Offline/Messaging onto it, deletes the old types and closes this finding (unblocks Jobs D2b).
findings.title: Actor identity is defined three times
findings.detail: Authorization.Public ActorKind + ActorIdentity, Audit.Public AuditActorKind + AuditActor + ActorRelation, Messaging.Rpc CallIdentity; Logging enriches its own user strings. ⚑RA8 (2026-11-04) decided the actor types go to core; ⚑RA10 'one ActorKind numbering' is still open, and Jobs D2b is blocked on it.
findings.recommendation: Do RA8 next: one ActorIdentity, ActorKind and real-actor relation in core; Audit, Rpc CallIdentity, Logging and Jobs map to it. Unblocks Jobs D2b and Audit implicit entries.

findings.title: Logging and Audit still invent machine identity instead of using Installations
findings.detail: Audit AuditTrail.NodeId = Guid.CreateVersion7() per process (a new node on every restart) and DeviceId is a free string; Logging LoggingOptions.DeviceId string + InstanceId Guid; Profiling has its own hardware fingerprint. Installations (I0–I5 built) exists precisely to be the one answer to 'which machine' (installations README §1).
findings.recommendation: Core contract 'current installation id' (types-only, already in YFex/src/YFex/Installations); Logging and Audit read it when present and fall back to a persisted id, never per-process.

findings.title: Three ways to send a message to a person
findings.detail: Authentication.Delivery (built: SMTP, HTTP e-mail, Twilio, Meta WhatsApp), Logging.Alerts (designed: own INotificationChannel/ISmsProvider), Jobs IJobNotifier (built, no-op). The Notifications plan addresses this but is still ⚑N1–N20 pending, while Authentication.Delivery keeps growing.
findings.recommendation: Approve Notifications before Logging Phase alerts and Jobs D2b; freeze new transports in Authentication.Delivery until it moves.

findings.title: Secret protection at rest has two contracts, one of them in the HTTP library
findings.detail: YFex.Web owns ISecretProtector + SecretLocation (location-bound, per-tenant keys) and SealedSecretProtector in Web.Data; YFex.Cryptography owns ISecretStore (Jobs.Templates.Cryptography uses it). Binding a secret to tenant/table/row is generic and needed by Jobs, Files, Notifications and Authentication.
findings.recommendation: Move ISecretProtector/SecretLocation/SealedSecretProtector to Cryptography (or Cryptography.Data); Web.Data consumes it; delete the obsolete AesSecretProtector.

findings.title: Outbox / inbox / journal / ledger re-implemented per library — candidate for one durable primitive
findings.detail: Built: Persistence IDurableQueue (deletes on dequeue, TTL, synchronous=NORMAL), Messaging.Rpc IOutbox/StorageBackedOutbox, Cqrs.Compensation ICommandJournal, Orchestration.Rpc IInbox, EventSourcing IEventInbox/KeyValueEventInbox, Offline ISiteJournal + IBrokerRequestLedger + IOfflineAllowanceLedger. Planned: Audit durable journal (⚑A13), Notifications outbox, Files Exchange ledger. Each has its own idempotency, retention and fsync policy.
findings.recommendation: New small design: durable append/claim/ack/dedupe primitives in Persistence (journal with idempotency key, retention policy, durability level) that the others compose. Do it before Audit A13, Notifications N-phases and Files F-phases start.

findings.title: Three schedulers / durable timers
findings.detail: Jobs SchedulerHost, Orchestration ISagaScheduler + KeyValueDelayScheduler (durable waits), DataMining WormScheduler. Hosting plans 'Jobs inside the host'.
findings.recommendation: Decide in Hosting H0 whether Orchestration's durable waits run on the Jobs scheduler or a shared durable-timer contract (part of the F09 primitive).

findings.title: UI contracts exist twice (core YFex.UI.Abstractions vs YFex.UI.Public)
findings.detail: YFex/src/UI/YFex.UI.Abstractions defines IDialog, IMessageBox, INavigation, INotification, IToast, Types — the same interfaces as YFex.UI/src/Core/YFex.UI.Public. Nothing references the core copy. YFex.Mvvm sits in the core repo but references YFex.UI.Public in another repo.
findings.recommendation: Delete the core copy; move YFex.Mvvm next to the UI components or keep it in core only if UI.Public moves to core.

findings.title: Localization: core message catalogs vs Capabilities' own localizer vs Delivery templates
findings.detail: Core has IMessageCatalog/MessageCatalog (Validation and the Notifications plan build on it). Capabilities defines ICapabilityLocalizer over Microsoft IStringLocalizer; Authentication.Delivery ships its own pt-BR/en/es templates.
findings.recommendation: Capabilities localizer as an adapter over IMessageCatalog; Delivery templates become catalog entries (moves with Notifications).

findings.title: Package naming conventions drift
findings.detail: Contracts: .Public (Audit, Authorization, Authentication, Search, UI) vs .Abstractions (Jobs, Jobs.Hub) vs core types. Generators: .Generator vs .SourceGenerator (Cqrs, NavigatR, Jobs, Xml) vs .Generators (Devices); test project YFex.CQRS.SourceGenerator.Tests (casing). DataMining connectors named YFex.Csv/Excel/MongoDb while engines are YFex.Data.Postgres. The Privacy repo holds only a generator (runtime types in core). Core type Percentual (Portuguese) among English names.
findings.recommendation: Pick .Public and .Generator ecosystem-wide; rename on the next breaking window; the atlas lists every project so the rename can be tracked.

findings.title: Platform coverage is uneven against the 'Windows/Linux/macOS' rule
findings.detail: Only Cryptography has .Linux/.Apple (written, not run). Installations, Time, Networking, System, Profiling, Security, Devices have .Windows only; Persistence embeds Windows CNG in an OS-neutral package. The projects table shows the platform packages per component.
findings.recommendation: Track a platform matrix per component (the atlas 'Platforms' column) and run linuxKit on each library's tests as an acceptance gate.

findings.title: Tenancy is optional for some libraries and hard-wired in others
findings.detail: Adapter packages: Cqrs.Tenancy, Persistence.Tenancy, Data.Tenancy. Direct references from the main package: Audit, Logging, Orchestration, Installations, Capabilities, Jobs.Abstractions, NavigatR, Messaging.Rpc, Resilience.Polly, Authorization, CustomLogic.
findings.recommendation: Move the ScopeIdentity value to core (like Installations/Time types). Tenancy keeps resolution and overrides; libraries need no adapter just to carry a scope.

findings.title: Machine information is spread over System, Profiling, Security, Devices and Networking
findings.detail: System NetworkSnapshot still exists next to Networking's snapshot (⚑N migration); Security.Windows references Profiling; YFex.System.Windows.Security lives in the core repo (YFex/src/System), not in YFex.System or YFex.Security.
findings.recommendation: Finish the Networking consumer migration for System; move YFex.System.Windows.Security to its repo; state System = machine facts, Devices = attached hardware, Profiling = behaviour, Security = inspection.

findings.title: ~20 source generators copy their helper code
findings.detail: docs/internal/source-generators.md documents copy-paste of shared helpers (EquatableArray, diagnostics, writers) into every netstandard2.0 generator.
findings.recommendation: A source-only shared package (linked Compile items from one folder, or a contentFiles package) keeps generators self-contained without drifting copies.

findings.title: Jobs' SQL store bypasses YFex.Data schema modules
findings.detail: DS-P3 moved Offline, Authentication and Rules tables to portable YFex.Data schema modules; YFex.Jobs.Persistence.EntityFrameworkCore defines its tables only through EF.
findings.recommendation: Declare the Jobs tables as a YFex.Data SchemaModule (EF still works through ApplyYFexModule).

findings.title: Every library ships hosted services, but there is no shared health/lifecycle contract yet
findings.detail: OutboxReplayer, ServerPermissionsFeed, Installations beacon/renewal, Offline connectivity/manifest/relay, SignedSnapshotRefresh, TimeSynchronizationService, NetworkConditionsMonitor, SchedulerHost… each reports status its own way. Hosting (status: proposed) is a prerequisite of Offline 4f.
findings.recommendation: Pull Hosting H0's module/health contract forward (types in core) so libraries report health the same way before more services are added.

findings.title: Design documents live in four places with two formats
findings.detail: New designs: YFex/docs/internal/<topic>/ with phases + acceptance + log. Jobs keeps Plans A/A2/B/C/D in its repo root + .opencode/rules; Devices and Web in repo docs/; older flat *-design.md files have no phase log and stale status lines.
findings.recommendation: atlas.json is the single index: each component names its design home; move superseded flat docs to an archive folder.

findings.title: Bridge packages are placed on either side, which creates component cycles
findings.detail: Authorization.Installations lives in Authorization (refs Installations) while Installations.Central refs Authorization.Public; Authentication.Offline lives in Authentication while Offline.Rules lives in Offline; Search.Capabilities, Capabilities.Cqrs, Jobs.Capabilities, Cqrs.Tenancy each pick a side.
findings.recommendation: Rule: a bridge A.B lives with the higher-level library of the pair and is named after it. The atlas flags any component cycle automatically.

findings.title: Domain neutrality holds in infrastructure code
findings.detail: No CPF/CNPJ/SEFAZ/Farma in infrastructure code paths — only in XML-doc examples and tests. Watch: Money/Currency/Percentual in core (fine as types), Cryptography.Xml profiles named after NF-e/eSocial, Time 'Authority' source used for SEFAZ (lives in Fiscal), Offline 'pharmacy scenarios' doc (examples).
findings.recommendation: Keep domain profiles in product packages; the scanner can add a grep rule if this regresses.

findings.title: Authorization and Messaging repos reference each other
findings.detail: YFex.Messaging.Rpc references YFex.Authorization, while YFex.Authorization.Installations (in the Authorization repo) references YFex.Messaging.Rpc. Surfaced by the F01 split on 2026-11-05; before it the edge pointed into the core repo.
findings.recommendation: Move YFex.Authorization.Installations out of the Authorization repo (e.g. into YFex.Installations or its own repo), or make Messaging.Rpc depend only on YFex.Authorization.Public.

findings.title: YFex.UI repo depends on the framework through the Gallery sample
findings.detail: YFex.Avalonia.Gallery (YFex.UI/src/Avalonia) references NavigatR, Mvvm, State.Mvvm and Validation, while NavigatR and Mvvm reference YFex.UI.Public: a repo cycle caused only by a sample app.
findings.recommendation: Move the Gallery to YFex.Mvvm/app (top layer).

findings.title: Per-scope configuration is about to be reinvented
findings.detail: Tenancy scoped overrides, Web per-scope endpoints/credentials, Notifications per-scope providers/templates, Hosting module profiles per scope, Installer release targeting per scope, Licensing activation lists per scope. Distribution already converges on Installations signed bundles (good); the resolution side does not.
findings.recommendation: One 'scoped settings' resolution contract in Tenancy (tenant → site → installation chain), used by Web, Notifications, Hosting and Installer; bundles stay the transport.
